facts.text: In 2025 there were 65 confirmed unprovoked shark bites on people worldwide, and 9 of them were deadly.
From 2020 to 2024 there were on average 61 unprovoked shark bites a year worldwide, and 8 unprovoked deaths a year.
In 2024 there were 47 unprovoked shark bites worldwide, 4 of them deadly.
In 2025 the United States had 25 unprovoked bites and Australia had 21; the yearly total remains extremely low.
At least 79 million sharks died in fisheries in 2019, up from about 76 million in 2012.
At least 25 million of the sharks killed in fisheries in 2019 belonged to threatened species.
People kill an estimated 80 million to 100 million sharks each year.
About one third of shark species are threatened with extinction.
Shark finning means cutting off a shark's fins and throwing the rest of its body back into the sea.
About 70 percent of countries and overseas territories have banned finning, but the total number of sharks killed has not gone down.
Sharks grow slowly, become adults late and have only a few young at a time, so many species are easily overfished.
Sharks keep the numbers of their prey in check and remove sick and weak animals, which helps keep the ocean healthy.
There are more than 500 species of sharks.
Taiwan requires sharks landed at its own ports to keep their fins attached to, or tied to, their bodies; the rule was announced in 2012.
Under Taiwan's rules for Pacific fishing, the fins on board may not be more than 5 percent of the total shark catch by weight.
At least 700 metric tons of shark fins are eaten in Taiwan each year, possibly from about 250,000 sharks.
In 2010 a group of Taiwanese groups asked four convenience store chains to stop selling shark fin dishes for Lunar New Year; the chains stopped in 2011.
In 2023 there were 69 confirmed unprovoked shark attacks worldwide.

notes: 具體事件：每年鯊魚咬人的件數（ISAF：2025 年 65 件無故咬人、9 件致死）對比人類每年捕殺的鯊魚數量（至少 7,900 萬隻，2019 年；估計每年 8,000 萬到 1 億隻）。批次提示建議的 FAO 來源沒有逐年捕殺隻數，改用 Science 2024 研究（經 National Geographic 報導）與 Taipei Times 的估計。
